name: Can you touch up baseboards and trim without repainting the whole room?

mainEntity.name: Can you touch up baseboards and trim without repainting the whole room?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, touching up trim requires specific techniques because trim, baseboards, and moldings usually have a semi-gloss or satin enamel finish, which shows lap marks easily. While flat wall paint absorbs light and conceals touch-ups well, higher-sheen trim paint reflects light and reveals brush strokes. For damaged baseboards or casings, lightly sand the nick, spot-prime bare wood, and brush a light coat feathered along the full length of that trim segment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but because trim uses higher-sheen enamel, touch-ups must be lightly sanded and feathered across that trim board segment to prevent visible brush marks.
